newsitem.title: USA: Cohen military budget challenged in Congress.
newsitem.headline: Cohen military budget challenged in Congress.

text.p: Defence Secretary William Cohen defended President Clinton's new military spending request to Congress Wednesday but a top Republican said it would lead the nation on a road "fraught with peril."

Representative Floyd Spence, the Republican chairman of the House National Security Committee, told Cohen the administration's $265 billion defence request would mean a smaller military force, spread thinner to meet U.S. commitments around the world.
"It is a road fraught with peril and one, unfortunately, that this nation has already been down with disastrous consequences several times this century," Spence said.

But Cohen told the committee the new request would pay for a military able to meet U.S. global commitments and said he would work hard for cooperation between the administration and Congress on defence spending.

"America must remain actively engaged in this complex global environment," he said. "We must exert strong leadership to deter aggression, foster peaceful resolution of conflicts, underpin stable foreign markets, encourage democracy and promote a better future for the community of nations."

Cohen, the first Republican in Clinton's Cabinet, told the Republican-controlled committee that "on matters of national defence, bipartisanship and cooperation are essential. Political consensus at home strengthens America's hand abroad."
